note: Working search query patterns discovered by the scout. WebFetch to individual ATS/board domains was blocked by the sandbox egress proxy on 2026-09-03; as of 2026-09-03 (later run same day) WebFetch to careers.google.com, bloomberg.avature.net, and job-boards.greenhouse.io worked directly (200s via curl too), but LinkedIn job-view pages, Workday SPA shells (myworkdayjobs.com), and janestreet.com/careers.twosigma.com sometimes block or fail to render for WebFetch even though curl gets HTTP 200 (JS-rendered content, or bot-detection redirect to a generic search page). Re-check egress/fetchability each run.
CRITICAL_LESSON_2026-09-03b: WebSearch result snippets/AI summaries are frequently WRONG or STALE: one run found a WebSearch summary claiming 'NYC' for a job whose actual page said 'Remote (Argentina)', and another claiming 'NYC option' for a job whose actual page said 'Toronto'. Separately, of 20 Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby/Wellfound/Dice URLs surfaced by WebSearch in one sweep, 16 were already-expired/removed postings (404, or a 302 redirect to the org's board root with ?error=true, or Ashby's embedded JSON showing posting:null) despite WebSearch presenting them as current results. ALWAYS WebFetch (or curl for a plain HTTP-status sanity check when WebFetch is blocked/renders nothing) each candidate URL before adding it to state / notifying on it, to confirm: (a) the posting still resolves live (not 404/redirect-to-error/posting:null), and (b) the actual title/location/seniority match, not just the search snippet's paraphrase. Do not trust an AI-generated WebSearch summary's location or seniority claims at face value. For Workday SPA shells that return 200 but render no content even via WebFetch, a plain curl HTTP status check (200 vs 404/500) is a reasonable fallback sanity check (X/Twitter's Workday job returned HTTP 500 this run and was excluded); still treat the URL's own auto-generated slug (title/location embedded in the path, e.g. .../New-York-NY/... or .../US-NY-Remote/...) as a reasonably reliable structured signal since ATS platforms generate slugs from the actual posting fields, not from an LLM paraphrase.
